evals.prompt: My Code 128 with 20 characters is 300 px wide in a 1920x1080 frame and doesn't scan. Why?
evals.expected_output: Counts modules (ppm_calc.py or the formula), computes PPM vs the 2–4 requirement and gives a target width.

assertions.text: The module count of the Code 128 is computed (ppm_calc.py ppm code128 --chars 20 --pixels 300, or the formula from code-readability.md)
A pixels-per-module number is given and compared with the 2–4 PPM requirement
A target width in pixels (or a smaller distance / higher resolution) is given to reach enough PPM
The answer asks for or mentions the original full-resolution frame rather than a screenshot

evals.prompt: Camera 1920 px wide, 70° horizontal field of view, 600 mm from the labels; the Code 128 X-dimension is 0.25 mm. Enough?
evals.expected_output: Uses ppm_calc.py plan (or the formula) to compute PPM at that distance and compares with 2–4; gives max distance or lens change.

assertions.text: ppm_calc.py plan --res-px 1920 --hfov 70 --distance-mm 600 --x-mm 0.25 (or the equivalent formula with steps) is used
A PPM value is stated and compared with the 2–4 requirement
A concrete improvement is given (shorter distance, narrower lens, higher resolution) with a target

evals.prompt: The Scandit app on my phone reads this label but my Linux single-image scanner doesn't. Same SDK, so why?
evals.expected_output: Video at close range with autofocus and many attempts vs one image; compare PPM and sharpness; HIGH_EFFORT, frame sequence per image; original frames.

assertions.text: The answer explains a phone scans a video stream at close range with autofocus and many attempts, a single image gets one try
The answer suggests comparing pixels per module and sharpness of the Linux frame
The answer checks single-image settings (SC_PRESET_HIGH_EFFORT, new frame sequence per image, duplicate filter off)
